record.original_question: For point vortices on non-orientable surfaces, can one study the first non-integrable small-vortex cases and describe both the full set of Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for area-preserving diffeomorphism groups, analogously to the orientable case?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider point vortices on a closed non-orientable surface $\Sigma$ (such as the real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle, or higher non-orientable surfaces) equipped with an area form induced from its orientable double cover. A configuration of $N$ point vortices with strengths $\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_N \in \mathbb{R}$ evolves by the Hamiltonian system on $\Sigma^N$ (minus collision and antipodal-image loci) whose Hamiltonian is the regularized Kirchhoff–Routh function obtained from the Green's function of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $\Sigma$.

(a) Identify the smallest values of $N$ for which the $N$-vortex problem on a non-orientable surface $\Sigma$ fails to be Liouville integrable, in analogy with the known integrable/non-integrable thresholds for vortices on the sphere, the plane, and the torus. In particular, determine whether the 3-vortex or 4-vortex problem on $\mathbb{RP}^2$ and on the Klein bottle is non-integrable, and exhibit explicit obstructions to integrability (e.g., transverse homoclinic intersections, Melnikov-type arguments, or symbolic dynamics).

(b) Describe the complete set of Casimir functions for the Lie–Poisson structure on the dual of the Lie algebra of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of $\Sigma$ (equivalently, a complete set of invariants of generic coadjoint orbits), in a manner analogous to the classification by generalized enstrophies and circulations on orientable surfaces, but accounting for the involution induced by the orientation double cover.

(c) Construct finite-dimensional approximations of the group $\mathrm{SDiff}(\Sigma)$ of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of $\Sigma$ (for instance by analogues of quantized tori or by skew-symmetric matrix models) whose Poisson brackets converge to the Lie–Poisson bracket on $\mathrm{SVect}(\Sigma)^*$, parallel to the existing $\mathfrak{su}(N)$-type approximations available in the orientable case.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has made substantial progress on parts of this program. A Hamiltonian formulation for point vortices on the Möbius band and on the Klein bottle has been developed, providing explicit Hamiltonians and equations of motion. Independently, coadjoint orbits of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces have been classified, with generalized enstrophies and circulations (refined by the orientation-cover involution acting on the vorticity Reeb graph) shown to form a complete set of invariants. However, explicit proofs of non-integrability for the first small-N cases, and explicit finite-dimensional matrix approximations of SDiff for non-orientable surfaces analogous to the orientable case, do not appear to be fully established, so the program is only partially complete.

status_evidence.title: Coadjoint orbits of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of generic coadjoint orbits of area-preserving diffeomorphisms on non-orientable surfaces; dimension of orbit space depends on involution action on the vorticity Reeb graph.
status_evidence.claim: Casimirs / coadjoint orbit classification for non-orientable surfaces has been carried out.

status_evidence.title: A Hamiltonian approach for point vortices on non-orientable surfaces II: the Klein bottle
status_evidence.snippet: Hamiltonian and equations of motion for one and two point vortices on the Klein bottle.
status_evidence.claim: Hamiltonian framework for small-N vortices on non-orientable surfaces (Möbius band, Klein bottle) is established.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Casimirs in 2D hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized enstrophies and circulations form a complete set of invariants of coadjoint orbits of area-preserving diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Casimir classification on orientable surfaces (and extensions) is known.
